sections.text: We ran two hundred and sixty-six recordings through a machine. Twenty-seven came back with the wrong product name in them.
You type up a call, forward the summary, and somebody acts on it. The page reads finished, so nobody rereads it. Nothing is underlined.
It does not fail at random. It fails on the parts that carry no context: proper nouns, figures, and anything said only once. The sentences around them stay clean.
So the check is small. Five fields, the same five every time. Names, numbers, dates, decisions, and who owes what. Here it is running against one of the bad files. There.

And here is what it does not catch on its own. When the machine writes a name as another real word every single time, the page still reads clean. So check the five against the recording, not against the page.
The five fields are in the caption, not behind a comment. Send this to whoever types up your calls.

strategy.audience: Non-technical small-business leader, AI level 0-6 of 10 (POSITIONING.md §4): an owner, operations lead or team lead in a 5-50 person company responsible for one repeated process. Specifically anyone turning calls, forms or documents into text that somebody else will act on.
strategy.concept: We put two hundred and sixty-six recordings through a machine transcriber and kept the mistakes in. Twenty-seven of them came back with the same product name written as a different, real word, and the sentences around it read perfectly. The reel gives away the five-field check we now run before machine-written text is forwarded, and then names the one failure the check cannot catch on its own.

filter.ai_boundary: The machine transcribes and extracts. A person checks a short, fixed list of fields against the source recording before the text moves on to anyone else; the person does not reread the page for sense, they check five named fields.
filter.friction: The machine-written page reads finished. It is wrong in exactly the places that carry no context - names, figures, anything said once - and because the sentences around the mistake are clean, nobody rereads a page that looks correct.
filter.next_action: Write down the five fields in your own documents that must never be wrong, and check only those, against the recording.
filter.process: Turning a recording or a document into text that another person will act on: the call summary, the meeting note, the intake form, the invoice line that gets typed up once a week and forwarded to somebody else.

strategy.objective: Get one viewer to write down the five fields in their own documents that must never be wrong, and to check those five against the recording rather than rereading the page.
strategy.promise: A fixed, five-field check on the step where a recording becomes text somebody acts on, plus an honest account of what that check still misses.
strategy.rationale: 84 of 266 analysed reels prove with a screen demo (I-18) and none of them shows a failure (reports/analysis/01-general-conclusions.md §G, writing rule 12: 'Nothing in the corpus shows a failure'); showing the same screen with the mistake left in is unrepresented in the corpus. Handing the artefact over instead of gating it is what the save evidence rewards: resource_handoff carries the corpus's highest save rate at 0.0429 (reports/analysis/01-general-conclusions.md §B), and the comment gate that usually carries it is banned by RULES.md §1.2 and buys no reach (I-12).

title: The wrong name in twenty-seven files

traceability.evidence_summary: Our own transcription run wrote 266 files and the per-file notes record 27 of them carrying the same product name as a different real word, with 191 of 266 notes discussing the transcription at all, 140 of them naming a specific word it got wrong, and 7 of 273 rows coming back empty. The failure is not spread evenly: it lands on proper nouns, figures and single mentions, which is what makes a fixed five-field check possible instead of a full reread. The four references supply structure only: DYC-x8DogOI (399.4x lift, 59.9 saves/1k) the result-plus-quantity opening, DcoE5ZsK4I7 (the pool's only CONSISTENT creator, 62.4 saves/1k) the claim-then-screen pacing, DMQMNNHSJRF (35.1 shares/1k) the volunteered limitation spoken over the screen, DWCPx0PkQzA (142.8x, 57.3 saves/1k) the teach-then-hand-over transition. The visual grammar follows I-09: the reel opens on the screen, where the 35 screen-first reels carry median share_rate 0.0213 against 0.0140 and the creator-normalised correlation (+0.285, p=0.00025) is stronger than the pooled one.
traceability.original_synthesis: The failure is ours, dated and reproducible from our own files, and the reel shows the broken output rather than the working one - which none of the 84 screen-demo reels in the analysed corpus does (01-general-conclusions §G, rule 12). The five-field check and the admission that it cannot catch a consistently mis-spelled name are both ours; nothing in the corpus states what its own method misses.
traceability.why_better_than_generic: A generic AI script would say 'always review AI output' and show the tool working. This one names the exact shape of the failure (proper nouns, figures, single mentions), gives away the artefact in the caption rather than gating it behind a comment - the gate is banned by RULES.md §1.2 and I-12 shows it buys no reach - and then closes by naming the one case the artefact cannot handle, which is the opposite of what a promotional script does.
